title: sweep() is the only native-asset exit and pays an attacker-chosen recipient instead of the ETH credit holders, so the whole ETH pool is permissionlessly extractable in one call
description: Discovery: Step 5b #4 (Value Flow Conservation) / Module O (payment destination correctness) / DP1-1 confirmed and deepened by Lens B. Tracing every wei of the native pool: the only function that ever moves ETH out is sweep(address payable to), which sends the entire address(this).balance to an arbitrary recipient chosen by the CALLER — not to the addresses credited via depositEth. No function ever pays ETH against balances[]. The recipient of the vault's ETH pool is therefore semantically wrong (arbitrary caller, not the asset holders), and because sweep is unguarded any address can take the whole pool. Deepened: the attacker can also recover their OWN depositEth funds through the same call — attacker sends 10 ETH via depositEth, calls withdraw(10e18) to steal 10e18 ERC20 units (DB-2), then calls sweep(attacker) to take all 10 ETH (plus anyone else's) back — so a depositEth→withdraw→sweep sequence nets stolen ERC20 tokens with ZERO net ETH outlay, and honest ETH depositors are left with unbacked ledger entries.
root_cause: The native-asset out-flow is a single permissionless whole-balance transfer to an arbitrary address, disconnected from the balances ledger; the payment destination is the caller's chosen `to` instead of the ETH credit holders, and there is no per-account ETH withdrawal to compete with it.

harm.who: all users who deposited native ETH via depositEth (and anyone who force-sent ETH to the vault)
harm.loses_what: their entire ETH balance held in the vault; also the round trip lets the attacker keep the ETH they used as the visible cost of a token theft
harm.magnitude: the full address(this).balance at call time — e.g. 10 ETH deposited by a victim is taken whole by the first sweeper; a 10 ETH depositEth→withdraw→sweep sequence extracts 10e18 ERC20 units at zero net ETH cost

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls depositEth{value: 10 ether}() → balances[victim] += 10e18; vault holds 10 ETH.
2. Attacker calls depositEth{value: 10 ether}() → balances[attacker] += 10e18.
3. Attacker calls withdraw(10e18) → ledger debited, vault pays 10e18 ERC20 units (victim's tokens, see DB-2) to the attacker.
4. Attacker calls sweep(attacker) → to.transfer(address(this).balance) returns the attacker's own 10 ETH plus the victim's 10 ETH (20 ETH) to the attacker; no guard exists.

5. Net: attacker holds their original 10 ETH + 10e18 stolen ERC20 units; victim's balances[victim] still reads 10e18 but vault ETH balance is 0 and withdraw() only pays ERC20 — victim's native deposit is irrecoverable.

preconditions.text: the vault holds any native ETH (any prior depositEth call or force-send)

postconditions.text: all native ETH held by the vault is owned by the attacker; honest ETH depositors' balances entries are unbacked
attacker retains an ERC20 withdrawal credit or has already converted it, so the ETH round trip leaves no residual cost

title: Unified balances ledger lets native-ETH credits (or unsolicited token donations) be redeemed 1:1 against other users' ERC20 deposits — dust ETH converts into full token units
description: Discovery: Module O #1 (trace each payment) / Step 5b #4 (value conservation) / vault-share-accounting §1 direct-donation vector / DP1-2 confirmed and deepened by Lens B. Accountant's wei trace: value IN = Σdeposit (ERC20) + ΣdepositEth (ETH); value OUT = Σwithdraw (ERC20 only) + sweep (all ETH, ungated). depositEth credits balances[] without taking custody of any token and without incrementing totalDeposits, while withdraw pays ERC20 for any credit regardless of how it was created — so 1 wei of native ETH buys 1 token unit (e.g. 1 wei ETH → 1 USDC base unit). Lens B deepening: a SECOND funding path exists that Pass 1 did not promote — ERC20 tokens transferred directly to the vault (unsolicited donation, no ledger credit) also become claimable through the same depositEth→withdraw redemption, because withdraw pays from the contract's raw token balance while debiting only the caller's ledger entry; totalDeposits and balanceOf(token) are never reconciled (no skim/sync). Combined with DB-1's ETH round trip the redemption is costless: depositEth → withdraw(token theft) → sweep(recover the ETH).
root_cause: A single untagged balances ledger backs two disjoint asset pools (ERC20 tokens and native ETH); withdraw always pays from the token pool, so any credit that did not arrive as tokens — ETH credits and untracked donations — is redeemable against other users' token deposits.

harm.who: ERC20 depositors (users who called deposit()) and direct token donors
harm.loses_what: their deposited tokens, paid out to whoever holds native-ETH credits or to the first redeemer of donated tokens
harm.magnitude: up to the vault's entire token balance — e.g. 1000 wei of ETH (dust, ~$0.003) redeems 1000 token units; with a 6-decimal token that is 0.001 whole tokens per 1000 wei, and the attacker recovers the ETH via sweep (DB-1) so the conversion repeats until the token pool is empty

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls deposit(1000e6) → balances[victim]=1000e6, totalDeposits=1000e6, vault holds 1000e6 tokens.
2. Attacker calls depositEth{value: 1000 wei}() → balances[attacker]=1000; no tokens enter; totalDeposits unchanged.

3. Attacker calls withdraw(1000) → balances check passes, unchecked totalDeposits decremented (may underflow, see DB-3), token.transfer(attacker, 1000) pays 1000 token units taken from the victim's deposit.
4. Attacker calls sweep(attacker) (DB-1) → recovers the 1000 wei ETH, so the theft costs nothing and can be repeated until the vault's token balance is 0.
5. Victim's later withdraw reverts on token.transfer (insolvent token pool) while balances[victim] still shows 1000e6.

Variant: anyone who directly transferred tokens to the vault (donation, no ledger credit) has those tokens claimed the same way by any depositEth credit holder — there is no skim/sync reconciling balanceOf(token) with totalDeposits.

preconditions.text: the vault holds ERC20 tokens deposited by other users (or donated directly)

postconditions.text: vault token balance falls below the sum of balances entries; later victim withdrawals revert
totalDeposits desynced from depositEth credits and from real token custody

recommendation: Separate the ledgers: depositEth must maintain an ETH-only accounting with a withdrawEth() that pays ETH, never ERC20; reconcile token custody (balanceOf(this) vs totalDeposits) with a skim/sync, and reject or attribute unsolicited transfers.

title: unchecked totalDeposits underflow in withdraw() wraps the counter and permanently DoS-es deposit() for normal amounts while destroying the accounting invariant
description: Discovery: Step 5b #4 (value conservation on the totalDeposits counter) / DP1-3 confirmed and deepened by Lens B. Accountant trace: totalDeposits is incremented only by deposit() but decremented by withdraw() against credits from ANY source; depositEth credits bypass the counter entirely, so sum(balances) can exceed totalDeposits and withdraw's unchecked subtraction wraps it to ~2^256. Lens B deepening: (a) the wrap is costless to the attacker because the same sequence recovers the ETH via sweep (DB-1) — economic cost bounds the wrap only if sweep is fixed; (b) after the wrap, deposit()'s checked totalDeposits += amount reverts once x > remaining headroom (headroom = 2^256 - wrapped value = amount_excess), so the core deposit function is DoS'd for any normal-size deposit; (c) balanceOf() and totalDeposits() now report meaningless values to any integrator, compounding the DB-2 desync.
root_cause: The unchecked subtraction is applied to a counter whose paired credits are bypassed by depositEth (and further decremented by donations never credited), so the invariant totalDeposits <= sum(balances) does not hold at withdrawal time.

harm.who: all users of the vault (depositors locked out of deposit), plus integrators reading totalDeposits
harm.loses_what: access to deposit() for any amount above the post-wrap overflow headroom; the totalDeposits accounting invariant; and the tokens paid out in the same transaction
harm.magnitude: after wrap with extra = amount - totalDeposits, every deposit(x) with x > extra reverts; deposits <= extra shrink headroom further; totalDeposits reads ~2^256 and is never reset by any code path

exploit_trace: 1. Victim calls deposit(100) → totalDeposits = 100; vault holds 100 tokens.
2. Attacker calls depositEth{value: 200 wei}() → balances[attacker] = 200; totalDeposits still 100.

3. Attacker calls withdraw(200): balances check passes; unchecked totalDeposits = 100 - 200 wraps to 2^256 - 100; token.transfer pays 200 token units to the attacker (100 of them the victim's, see DB-2).
4. totalDeposits now reads 2^256 - 100. Every subsequent deposit(x) with x > 100 reverts on checked totalDeposits += x; deposits <= 100 succeed and shrink the headroom.
5. No code path ever resets totalDeposits; the wrapped value persists forever and totalDeposits/balanceOf report garbage.

preconditions.text: permissionless depositEth creates balances credits that bypass totalDeposits
vault holds enough ERC20 tokens for token.transfer to succeed so the wrapped state persists (obtainable via DB-2)

postconditions.text: totalDeposits wrapped to ~2^256; deposit() reverts for amounts above remaining headroom
public totalDeposits()/balanceOf() report values decoupled from any real asset, breaking integrator assumptions

recommendation: Remove the unchecked block (let the subtraction revert) and decrement totalDeposits only in proportion to token-denominated deposits, or replace the counter with token.balanceOf(address(this)) accounting reconciled via skim/sync.

title: depositEth has no per-account ETH withdrawal path at all — native credits can only leave via whole-balance sweep, so honest depositors' ETH is lost to the first sweeper (and would be permanently locked if sweep were onlyOwner-patched)
description: Discovery: Step 5b #4 (value in must equal value out per user) / Module W-adjacent missing-functionality seen from the value-flow side / new in Lens B (Pass 1 covered the missing guard on sweep, not the missing exit for depositEth). Value-flow conservation for the native pool: depositEth is the ONLY way ETH enters, and NO function ever pays ETH to a balance holder — withdraw() pays ERC20 exclusively. Therefore native credits have exactly one exit: the permissionless whole-balance sweep, which is a race — with two honest depositors A (10 ETH) and B (10 ETH), the first to call sweep(self) takes 20 ETH and the second gets 0; the loser suffers permanent, non-error fund loss even with zero malice anywhere in the system. The obvious fix for DB-1 (add onlyOwner to sweep) does NOT restore value conservation: it converts theft into permanent lock, since owner has no per-user payout either. This root cause (missing withdrawEth/exit path) survives the access-control patch and must be fixed alongside it.
root_cause: The native-asset leg of the ledger is one-way: value enters via depositEth but no withdrawEth()/refund path exists that debits balances[user] and pays ETH to that user; the only ETH out-flow is an all-or-nothing sweep of the pooled balance.

harm.who: every honest depositor who funds via depositEth, specifically the ones who lose the sweep race or who rely on a post-patch sweep
harm.loses_what: their entire native-ETH deposit — taken by the first sweeper today, or permanently locked if sweep is restricted without adding a per-user ETH withdrawal
harm.magnitude: the loser's full deposit — e.g. with two depositors of 10 ETH each, one walks away with 20 ETH and the other with 0; under a naive onlyOwner fix to sweep, 100% of all depositEth funds become irrecoverable

exploit_trace: 1. A calls depositEth{value: 10 ether}(); B calls depositEth{value: 10 ether}(). Vault holds 20 ETH, balances A=10e18, B=10e18.

2. There is no withdrawEth or per-account payout function — inspect every state-changing function: deposit (ERC20 in), depositEth (ETH in), sweep (all ETH out to arbitrary `to`), withdraw (ERC20 out). ETH can only leave through sweep.
3. A calls sweep(A) (permissionless): to.transfer(address(this).balance) sends the full 20 ETH to A. balances[B] still reads 10e18 but the vault holds 0 ETH.
4. B calls sweep(B): balance is 0, transfer(0) succeeds, B receives nothing. B's 10 ETH is permanently gone with no malice required — pure race loss.

5. Alternative world: deployer patches DB-1 by adding onlyOwner to sweep. Now step 3/4 are impossible for A/B, but no function exists that pays B his 10 ETH either — B's deposit is permanently locked (worse outcome than the race).

preconditions.text: at least one depositEth call credited native value to balances
at least two ETH depositors (or any competing sweeper) for the race variant; onlyOwner-patched sweep for the lock variant

postconditions.text: the sweep-race loser's balances entry is permanently unbacked by ETH with no redemption path
under an access-control-only fix of sweep, all ETH deposits become permanently inaccessible (fund lock)
